source: J. Naylor (G4KLX), 'The Format of D-Star Slow Data' v0.2, 2009-03-10, hex tables of real-radio dumps (credited there to a third party); read 2026-11-06. Only the block layout is kept here: the strings in those dumps hold a personal callsign and position and are NOT copied. Hex is descrambled, one block = 6 bytes.

header.note: radio header resend: 8 x 0x55 + 0x51 (the 41st byte), then the filler block

gga.note: $GPGGA ... *hh CR LF; the last block 0x31 holds the LF

rmc.note: $GPRMC ... *hh CR LF; the last block 0x34 holds 4 characters (2 checksum digits, CR, LF)

dprs.note: $$CRCxxxx,<APRS string> CR: 17 blocks, so two superframes

squelch.note: code squelch 19: c2 19 19 then filler (the only example without personal data, kept in full)
